correctness.rationale: From the path-algebra multiplication, [x,y]_e=(a_u-a_v)s_e-(b_u-b_v)r_e, and diagonal/radical cross terms are the only products surviving modulo J². For ℓ commutators, the 2ℓ diagonal coordinates label vertices with q^(2ℓ) colors; supported edges must connect distinct labels. A proper labeling conversely independently solves each supported arrow coefficient, proving minimum length including z=0 and isolated vertices. For each diagonal coloring the linear coefficient map has q or q² solutions per arrow, leading to the exact fiber and FK expansion. Nonnegative-leading-coefficient state sums prove the asymptotic and Nash-Williams supplies its two-forest interpretation. The three replayable checkers directly enumerate finite field commutators and compare all target fibers/width tests; no experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2014 radical-square-zero algebra paper treats module geometry; Sokal 2005 already proves the combinatorial Potts/FK polynomial, credited; the available published two-vertex Kronecker paper already has its special-case commutator fibers, also credited. Full relevant sources were examined. The new item is the mapping of all support-specific additive commutators to graph colorings, exact length and general fibers, including unbounded width and forest-threshold probability, not a novel Tutte polynomial. No located stronger prior theorem directly implies it, but an unindexed bilinear-map interpretation remains a priority risk.

value.rationale: The additive-commutator width and fiber distribution are intrinsic, natural invariants of finite associative algebras. The uniform formula translates a nonlinear commutator-image problem into graph coloring, allows arbitrarily large widths in simple finite-dimensional quiver families, and quantitatively relates commuting probability to arboricity; these are structural features invisible in the known two-vertex counts. The result is not merely a field-size substitution or an arbitrary finite slice.
